I imagine this is going to be marketing more than anything else. I expect a fairly strong attack on VR from traditional media industries for similar reasons to why alcohol companies are so vehemently opposed to the legalization of marijuana. I think they're ultimately going to be pissing into the wind regardless of what happens but painting the device as a glorified porn tool right off the bat could be an effective attack, even if only temporarily. I'm curious what Facebook will do once they get an established userbase where the media and marketing no longer really matters. They'll definitely want to cash in on the porn, but "obscenity" laws in the US tend to be complex and vary radically from state to state.

There's also the issue of third party apps. In my opinion Oculus is going to be forced to allow anything to run on their hardware. The reason is simply competition. There's a lot of companies making VR hardware and one is ultimately going to come out on top. If Oculus tries to restrict what can run on their hardware then it's probably not going to be them. On the other hand their monetization idea seems to be relying on an exclusive storefront. Allowing people to run anything from anywhere would at least ostensibly hurt this. It'll be interesting to see what develops.

It looks like this is one of those times when the Gizmodo article is actually somewhat more illuminating. Here's an archived copy.

This paragraph in particular makes it seem they're pretty confident that the Rift itself will still be able to run unapproved programs.

Technically, there’s something to Oculus’s statement. In some sense, the Oculus Rift is just a fancy display hooked up to a Windows PC. You can run whatever you want. But depending on how integral Oculus’s own interface is to the actual experience, the official Oculus Store might have a chilling effect on non-approved content.

So, there's going to be an Oculus app store, and it's going to be locked down, apparently primarily for the purpose of ensuring the games run well enough to prevent nausea. This doesn't necessarily mean that the actual device will only be able to run Oculus approved apps, just that the official store won't be selling them. People wishing to purchase such content will likely just need to deal with the producers more directly, and as such be at their mercy with regard to the quality of their VR experience. I don't know how much of a problem that might turn out to be. Of course, this all relies on the platform remaining open beyond the walls of their app store.

I mentioned earlier, there really isn't anything proprietary about their interface. The SDK is just Unity and some libraries, IIRC. Anybody can just make stuff for the Rift, they just may not be able to publish it to their app store. It's not like early Android an iPhones where the only way to install software is through their app store, it's more like todays phones where you can just get the apk and put it on your phone.

I almost wonder how long it'll be before an f.droid-like store for the Rift appears for this kind of fringe stuff.

34 Truths People Who Get Migraines Wish Others Understood

9

“For the sake of others, you usually pretend you feel much better than you actually do.”

1. “One can look functional while in a lot of pain. Not all migraines develop into the hang-over-the-bowl, turn-out-the-lights, don’t-speak-to-me-for-four-days kind. We take care of our kids, go to work (mostly) and even drive carpool to school while quite ill.” — Nancy Roko

Uh, this one bothers me a lot. Yes there are times when my migraines incapacitating (and it's god awful when it happens). But if I were to drop everything, cancel my plans and go home sick every time my pain levels went above 5 I would have no life whatsoever - there's no way I would have completed school, hold a job, have any social life and at it's worse even leave the house.

The thing with chronic pain is... you get used to it.

Yes, I can be eating out with you, with a smile on my face, nodding along yet be in horrific pain, not be able to read the menu and struggle to use a knife and fork. Heck, I wrote 3 essays for my final english exam with a 6/10 migraine, I couldn't help but laugh at how surreal that experience was. If this wasn't my normal I would probably be locked up in my room for days.
